title: Do I need to accept a repair for faulty item?
body:
O.P.
Hello,
Bit of a long story sorry.
I purchased an LG robot vacuum in July 2024. About 6 months of ownership it began to have a few issues so reached out to LG who stated we needed to take it to a repair centre and if they found no issue we would be liable for the cost. Due to this and me not being aware of our consumer rights we didn’t want to take it and have to potentially pay the cost so we lived with the issues.
However issues got progressively worse over time so I left a review on the product page only to find out that the item is now discontinued after only being on the market for a year or so (assuming this is because there was so many issues) LG reached out after my review and stated from the videos I sent that the unit is faulty and believe it can be effectively repaired. However now that the unit is discontinued and previous reports from other owners that issues were still present after being sent for repair I do not want to settle for a repair and believe a refund is the only acceptable outcome. Do I have to accept a repair as the solution?
The store that sold it to us is requesting a RA number from LG so they can process the refund but LG are refusing to give us an RA number.
Thanks very much.

---- replies ----
[User #1247826177 postsbentlegyep, they are all bentWhirlpool Forums Addict] southy33 writes...
Do I have to accept a repair as the solution?
Yes.
Consumer law is that a defect must be repaired, replaced or replaced with something equivalent.
[User #18356030298 postspgdownloadWhirlpool Forums Addict] southy33 writes...
and me not being aware of our consumer rights
You're still not really aware of you're rights. They cut both ways and are designed not to be absolute but provide a reasonable remedy.
who stated we needed to take it to a repair centre and if they found no issue we would be liable for the cost.
You are still liable for the cost under ACL (Australian Consumer Law) if there is no fault and it is entirely reasonable that the company be able to inspect the goods to confirm the fault before they accept your word on the matter (people get it wrong).
Do I have to accept a repair as the solution?
As a first step, generally yes. They'll inspect and one of the loopholes in ACL is they can fix it and then you have nothing to complain about. There is literally no longer a "fault".
Now you can keep insisting on a refund but that may involve months of waiting, going to small claims and no certainty of an outcome you want. If its a $10K vacuum it might be worth it. If not then probably not.
At this stage I'd recommend you take the offer on the table and if the vacuum fails again then you have a much stronger case for a refund.
[User #91200748 postssouthy33Participant] O.P.
Perfect.
Thanks very much for your reply, I emailed them today to request the service centre location so hopefully can all get sorted :)
Appreciate it!
